bib.title: EfficientRAG: Efficient Retriever for Multi-Hop Question Answering
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v2, 26 Sep 2024); the PDF names no venue

read.skipped: reference list and prompt appendix tables (Tables 7-22) skimmed

question: Can multi-hop retrieval iterate without an LLM call per hop?
hypothesis: The relations in multi-hop questions are few, so a small token classifier can pick the useful span from a retrieved chunk and rewrite the next-hop query, replacing the LLM calls of iterative RAG.
contributions: A Labeler and Tagger (marks useful tokens, tags the chunk Continue or Terminate) and a Filter (builds the next query from the question plus labelled tokens), both token classifiers
A synthetic training set built with Llama-3-70B: decomposition, token labelling, next-hop question, hard negatives
Retrieval, QA and latency comparison with Iter-RetGen and SelfAsk on three multi-hop datasets

method.summary: Retrieve with Contriever-MSMARCO. The Labeler annotates useful tokens in each chunk and tags it Continue or Terminate; Continue chunks join a candidate pool. The Filter concatenates the question and the labelled tokens and extracts the next-hop query tokens. Loop until all chunks are Terminate or the iteration cap; then one LLM call answers over the pool.

datasets.name: HotpotQA, MuSiQue, 2WikiMQA
datasets.preprocessing: Llama-3-70B-Instruct generated decompositions, token labels, next-hop questions; hard negatives retrieved as most similar irrelevant chunk

models.name: EfficientRAG Labeler and Filter
models.architecture: DeBERTa-v3-large, 24 layers, linear heads for token labels and chunk tag

metrics.name: LLM calls, iterations, latency, GPU utilisation

eval.protocol: single runs; baselines run from source code with Llama-3-8B-Instruct

results.claim: On HotpotQA EfficientRAG reaches Recall 81.84 while retrieving 6.41 chunks on average, against Direct-R@30 77.05 at 30 chunks and Iter-RetGen iter3 83.05 at 16.42; on 2WikiMQA 84.08 at 3.69 chunks against SelfAsk 88.90 at 33.68.
On MuSiQue EfficientRAG recall is low: 49.51 at 6.09 chunks against Direct-R@10 50.86 and Decompose-R 67.23.
results.note: authors call the result less satisfactory

results.claim: End to end with a Llama-3-8B reader, EfficientRAG Acc is 57.86 on HotpotQA (Iter-RetGen iter2 59.29), 20.00 on MuSiQue (SelfAsk 26.97, Iter-RetGen iter2 26.28) and 53.41 on 2WikiMQA (SelfAsk 55.16): second best on two datasets and not the best on any.
results.note: the abstract says it surpasses existing RAG methods; Table 3 shows it second best on two datasets and below Iter-RetGen and SelfAsk on MuSiQue

results.claim: On 200 MuSiQue samples EfficientRAG uses 1.00 LLM calls, 2.73 iterations and 3.62 s latency, against Iter-RetGen iter3 3.00 calls and 9.68 s and SelfAsk 7.18 calls and 27.47 s.
results.note: authors state a 60%-80% time improvement over other iterative methods

results.claim: With a GPT-3.5-turbo-1106 reader on 2WikiMQA EfficientRAG Acc is 61.88 against Iter-RetGen iter3 60.60.
Trained on one dataset and tested on the other, Acc is 53.38 (HotpotQA test, 2WikiMQA-trained) and 56.59 (2WikiMQA test, HotpotQA-trained) against 57.86 and 53.41 in-domain.

Empirical study: with oracle chunks the reader beats direct answering, and adding irrelevant chunks (mixed) still lowers accuracy relative to oracle chunks, for GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and Llama-3-8B on 2WikiMQA.
results.quote: the presence of irrelevant chunks continues to challenge the LLM generator

limits: Only Llama-3-8B (and GPT-3.5 on one dataset) as reader; no larger LLM reader tested.
Open-domain multi-hop datasets only; no in-domain or enterprise corpus.
Training data comes from a 70B LLM and is dataset-specific; transfer was tested only between HotpotQA and 2WikiMQA.
Recall on MuSiQue is low and end-to-end accuracy trails Iter-RetGen and SelfAsk there.
Latency measured on 200 samples from one dataset.
